obligations_applied.Description: internal_promotion: Pay-range posting (if promotion creates new or changed role): If promotion creates a new title or materially changes the role and employer has 30+ employees, system must flag that any new job posting for that role must include salary range per § 181.173 (effective 2025-01-01, enacted by the 2024 Omnibus Labor and Industry Policy Bill, SF 3852). Correction (2026-09-03 contradiction closure): § 181.9414 was repealed effective 2021 (2020 Minn. Stat., amended 1Sp2021 c.10 art.3 s.22) and is not the pay-range posting statute; the operative citation is § 181.173, consistent with the Summary and § 4 above. "Salary range" = employer's reasonable estimate of hourly rate or annual salary for the position. If new title is not posted externally, no posting requirement. Recommendations: (1) integrate salary-range requirement into job-posting workflow; (2) flag roles that have never had a salary range posted; (3) require range to be entered before job posting goes live.

obligations_applied.Description: Non-compete void notice: If employee has pre-existing non-compete agreement in file, promotion should not trigger re-signing, re-confirmation, or enforcement of the non-compete. System should generate compliance note: "Non-compete per Minn. Stat. § 181.988 is void unless related to sale of business or business dissolution. No non-compete enforcement on role change or promotion. Do not require employee to re-sign non-compete." If system encounters a non-compete flag on employee record during promotion, escalate to legal for review; do not proceed with re-signing.

Citation.Note: Non-compete void notice: If employee has pre-existing non-compete agreement in file, promotion should not trigger re-signing, re-confirmation, or enforcement of the non-compete.

obligations_applied.Description: OVERTIME_THRESHOLD test: Overtime classification review: If promotion moves employee from overtime-eligible (48-hour threshold under § 177.25) to exempt classification, system must trigger a review workflow: (1) verify that § 177.21 exemption criteria are met (executive, administrative, professional duties test—not merely salary-based); (2) require manager attestation that role duties meet exemption standard; (3) document duties change in personnel file; (4) do not rely on salary alone for exemption. Conversely, if promotion moves exempt to non-exempt, recalculate overtime eligibility. System should flag if classification change lacks documented duties justification.
